brief.title: Ring attention
brief.audience: A curious reader unfamiliar with the concept; comfortable with simple diagrams, but with no machine-learning or distributed-systems background.
brief.learning_objective: After watching, the learner can explain the one key mechanism of ring attention: a long sequence is cut into shards spread across devices linked in a ring, each device keeps its queries local, and the key/value blocks travel around the ring so every device attends to every block - full attention without any device holding the whole key/value data.
prerequisites: A sequence is processed token by token (a token is one unit of text); introduced on screen before use.
Attention matches each token's query against every token's key and combines every value; introduced on screen before the mechanism starts.
A device is one processor with its own limited memory; introduced on screen before the memory problem is shown.

terms.definition: One unit of text the model processes.
The transformer step where each token gathers information from every other token by matching its query against keys and combining values.
The role vector a token uses to state what it is looking for in the other tokens.
The role vector a token offers for matching against queries.
The role vector holding the content a token contributes when others attend to it.
One processor with its own private memory, such as one accelerator chip.
One consecutive piece of the sequence, stored on one device.
The keys and values belonging to one sequence shard; the unit that travels around the ring.
The closed-loop layout in which every device exchanges data only with its two neighbors.
The running per-query record of what the key/value blocks that have visited a device contributed so far.

brief.core_claim: Ring attention cuts a long sequence into shards stored on devices linked in a ring; each device keeps its queries local while key/value blocks travel the ring, and after one full loop every device has attended to the whole sequence without any device ever holding the whole key/value data.

mechanism.description: Attention requires every token's query to meet every token's key and value.
For a very long sequence, the keys and values together outgrow one device's memory.
The sequence is cut into consecutive shards and each device stores one shard, including its key/value block.
The devices are linked in one closed ring, and each device exchanges data only with its two neighbors.
Each device keeps its queries at home; only the key/value blocks travel.
In lockstep, every device sends its held key/value block to one neighbor and receives another block from its other neighbor.
When a block visits a device, the device computes the attention between its local queries and that block and adds the contribution to its partial attention result.
After one full loop, every block has visited every device; the partial results merge into the same attention as if the whole sequence were on one device.

claims.statement: Attention matches each token's query against every token's key and combines every value, so every query needs access to every key and value.
qualifications: This describes the standard transformer attention requirement; the video shows the requirement, not the arithmetic.

claims.statement: The keys and values for a whole sequence grow with the sequence length and can become too large for one device's memory.
qualifications: Whether the data exceeds a device depends on the sequence, the model, and the device; this video claims no specific sizes, counts, or numbers.

claims.statement: Ring attention cuts the sequence into consecutive shards and stores one shard per device.
qualifications: The four devices shown are an illustrative layout, not a recommended or measured configuration.

claims.statement: The devices are connected in one closed loop, and each device exchanges data only with its two neighbors.
Each device keeps its own queries at home; only the key/value blocks travel around the ring.
When a key/value block visits a device, the device computes the attention between its local queries and that block, and adds the result to a running partial attention result.
qualifications: The coverage dots and partial-result bars in the animation are illustrative indicators of progress, not measured quantities.

claims.statement: After one full loop, every device has combined its queries with every key/value block, giving the same attention as if the whole sequence were on one device.
qualifications: The equivalence holds in exact arithmetic; real floating-point rounding can introduce tiny differences.

claims.statement: No device ever holds the whole sequence's keys and values at once.
Attention itself is unchanged; only the arrangement of the computation across devices changes.

example.summary: A four-device ring holding four sequence shards (illustrative layout).
example.detail: Four devices each store one shard's key/value block. Each device keeps its own block and receives the other three in turn as the blocks circulate.
example.calculation: 4 shards in total; each device sees its own 1 block + 3 received blocks = 4 blocks, which is every block; each block makes 3 hops, so one full loop suffices. The device count is an illustrative layout choice, not a measured configuration.

must_preserve: The negation: attention itself is unchanged - only the arrangement of computation across devices changes.
No performance numbers appear on screen; every size relationship stays qualitative.
The four-device ring and the shard layout are illustrative, not a measured or recommended configuration.
Whether the key/value data exceeds one device depends on the sequence, the model, and the device; no specific sizes are claimed.
The equivalence to single-device attention holds in exact arithmetic; floating-point rounding can introduce tiny differences.
omissions: Training details and load balancing for shards of unequal size.
Overlapping versus non-overlapping communication schedules and their costs.
The exact arithmetic that merges partial attention results (online rescaling of attention weights).
Concrete implementations, hardware, benchmarks, or performance figures.

The four key/value blocks hop around the ring in synchronized steps with eased motion; at every arrival the visiting block briefly flashes against that device's queries, one coverage dot fills, and the partial-result bar grows. One tracked block is drawn bolder so the eye can follow a single journey.
